Apple___Apple_scab.about: Olive-green to dark scabby spots on leaves and fruit, worst in cool, wet springs.
actions: Rake and destroy fallen leaves to reduce spores
Prune to improve air flow through the canopy
Apply a recommended fungicide from bud break in wet weather

Apple___Black_rot.about: Purple-edged leaf spots ('frog-eye'), rotting fruit and cankers on branches.
actions: Remove mummified fruit and dead or cankered wood
Keep the orchard floor clean
Use a recommended fungicide during the growing season

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.about: Bright orange-yellow leaf spots; the fungus alternates between apple and juniper/cedar trees.
actions: Remove nearby juniper/cedar hosts where practical
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties
Apply a protective fungicide in spring

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.about: White powdery growth on young leaves, which may curl and distort.
actions: Prune for better air circulation and sunlight
Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser
Apply sulphur or another recommended fungicide early

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.about: Long rectangular grey-tan lesions between leaf veins; favoured by warm, humid weather.
actions: Rotate with non-host crops
Plough under or remove crop residue
Use tolerant hybrids; consider fungicide if severe

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.about: Small cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces.
actions: Plant resistant hybrids
Scout regularly during cool, humid periods
Apply fungicide only if infection is heavy early in the season

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.about: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on leaves.
actions: Use resistant hybrids
Rotate crops and manage residue
Consider fungicide at early tasseling if disease is spreading

Grape___Black_rot.about: Brown leaf spots with dark borders; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
actions: Remove mummified berries and infected canes
Improve air flow with canopy management
Apply a protective fungicide from early shoot growth

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).about: Tiger-stripe yellowing between veins and dark spotting on berries; caused by wood-rotting fungi.
actions: Prune out and destroy infected wood
Protect large pruning wounds
Prune in dry weather to limit infection

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.about: Dark brown irregular leaf spots that can cause early leaf drop.
actions: Remove infected leaves and debris
Improve canopy ventilation
Apply a recommended fungicide if widespread

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).about: Blotchy yellow mottling of leaves, lopsided bitter fruit; there is no cure.
actions: Remove and destroy infected trees to protect others
Control the Asian citrus psyllid insect
Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock

Peach___Bacterial_spot.about: Small angular water-soaked spots that turn purple-brown; leaves may look shot-holed.
actions: Plant resistant varieties
Avoid overhead irrigation
Use copper sprays as advised locally

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.about: Small dark water-soaked leaf spots that turn brown; spreads in warm, wet weather.
actions: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
Avoid overhead watering and working with wet plants
Rotate crops; copper sprays can slow spread

Potato___Early_blight.about: Brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern), usually on older lower leaves first.
actions: Remove infected lower leaves
Rotate crops and keep plants well nourished
Apply a recommended fungicide if spreading

Potato___Late_blight.about: Dark water-soaked patches with pale edges; spreads very fast in cool, wet weather.
actions: Act quickly: remove and destroy infected plants
Avoid overhead watering
Apply a recommended fungicide and warn nearby growers

Squash___Powdery_mildew.about: White powdery patches on leaves and stems that reduce yield.
actions: Space plants for good air flow
Remove badly infected leaves
Use resistant varieties or sulphur/potassium bicarbonate sprays

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.about: Many small purple spots that merge until the leaf looks scorched.
actions: Remove infected leaves after harvest
Avoid overhead watering
Renovate or replant beds with healthy plants

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.about: Small dark greasy spots on leaves and fruit, favoured by warm, wet weather.
actions: Use disease-free seed and transplants
Avoid overhead watering
Rotate crops; copper sprays can reduce spread

Tomato___Early_blight.about: Brown spots with target-like rings on older leaves, often with a yellow halo.
actions: Remove infected lower leaves
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves
Rotate crops; apply a recommended fungicide if needed

Tomato___Late_blight.about: Large greasy grey-green patches that spread very quickly in cool, humid weather.
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Keep foliage dry and well spaced
Apply a recommended fungicide preventively in risky weather

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.about: Pale yellow spots on the upper leaf surface with olive-green mould underneath; common in humid greenhouses.
actions: Reduce humidity and improve ventilation
Avoid wetting the leaves
Remove infected leaves; use resistant varieties

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.about: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey centres on lower leaves.
actions: Remove infected leaves
Mulch and water at the base of plants
Rotate crops; apply a recommended fungicide if spreading

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.about: Fine yellow speckling on leaves, sometimes with fine webbing; worse in hot, dry conditions.
actions: Spray leaves with water to knock mites off
Encourage natural predators
Use insecticidal soap or a recommended miticide

Tomato___Target_Spot.about: Brown spots with concentric rings on leaves, stems and fruit.
actions: Improve air flow by pruning and spacing
Remove crop debris after harvest
Apply a recommended fungicide if needed

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.about: Upward-curling, yellowing leaves and stunted plants with poor fruit set.
actions: Remove infected plants
Control whiteflies (yellow sticky traps, insect netting)
Plant resistant varieties

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.about: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, with distorted growth.
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants
Disinfect tools and wash hands; the virus spreads by touch
Use resistant varieties and certified seed
